parole.testo: Learned borrowing from French acardie. See Late Latin acardia < a- privative + -cardia, formed on Ancient Greek ἀ- (a-, “-less”) + κᾰρδῐ́ᾱ (kărdĭ́ā, “heart”) + -ῐ́ᾱ (-ĭ́ā, suffix forming abstract nouns). Equivalent to α- (a-) + καρδ(ιά) (kard(iá)) + -ία (-ía).

parole.significato: prosthesis (an artificial replacement for a body part)
parole.testo: From French prothèse, from Late Latin prothesis, prosthesis, from Koine Greek πρόσθεσις (prósthesis, “addition of a letter to the beginning of a word”).
